clips.title: The story
paras: Flutterfly Dust is a local task in the Gustberry Lowlands involving the harvesting of powder from giant, winged flutterflies. While the insects are usually docile, isolated homesteaders rely on travelers to gather the messy substance due to the constant threat of roving bandits.

The outer fields and orchards of the Gustberry Lowlands are home to giant flutterflies, picturesque winged insects that drift lazily through the rural landscape. While their gentle appearance lends a pastoral charm to the area, their fluttering wings shed a fine, pervasive dust that can be gathered in bulk. Though primarily wild insects, their presence draws the attention of nearby homesteaders who seek to harvest this airborne byproduct for practical domestic needs.

Harvesting flutterfly dust requires a surprisingly blunt approach: striking the large insects with a Flutterfly Swatter. Most flutterflies simply panic and take to the air when struck, shaking their rumps and dropping piles of loose powder behind them. Occasionally, however, an agitated flutterfly will turn and strike back when provoked, proving that even docile garden bugs have their limits when swatted.

Collecting the dust is a messy, clinging endeavor that tends to coat clothing and gear for weeks. While the local requester eagerly awaits the delivery due to lurking bandits making solo trips into the fields too dangerous, the final destination of the dust is kept tightly under wraps. Pressed on how it will be used, the homesteader only offers evasive dismissals about general 'stuff and things.'

clips.title: Quest text
paras: I'm sure you've noticed the giant flutterflies out in the outer fields near the orchard? They are pleasant to look at, but they also have other benefits; namely their wing dust. It can be a mess, but if you can gather it up in large amounts, it has useful household applications.

Take this Flutterfly Swatter and give the big bugs a good swat for me. They'll usually just get scared and flee, but sometimes they'll take some offense. Either way, they'll give their rumps a shake and drop a pile of dust.

clips.title: Progress
paras: Flutterflies are normally docile and calm, but rub them the wrong way and sometimes they'll surprise you.

clips.title: Completion
paras: This stuff can be a bit messy and it tends to get everywhere. You'll probably be shaking this out of your trousers for weeks, unfortunately. I do appreciate it, though. I've had this on my to-do list for weeks, but getting too far from the house when it's just me on my own with bandits lurking everywhere is a big risk.
Don't bother asking me what I use this stuff for. Things. Stuff and things. Don't worry about it.
